text.p: HealthSouth Corp and Horizon/CMS Healthcare Corp said Tuesday they have definitively agreed to merge in a stock pact valued at about $1.6 billion, including the assumption of about $700 million in debt.
The merger gives stockholders of Horizon/CMS 0.42169 a share of HealthSouth for each share of Horizon/CMS common stock, the companies said.
The merger combines the nation's largest network of rehabilitation facilities, HealthSouth, with the second-largest, Horizon/CMS.
HealthSouth said it expects the acquisition to be accretive to 1997 earnings per share.
"We are very excited to add the rehabilitation operations of Horizon/CMS," HealthSouth Chairman and Chief Executive Richard Scrushy said in a release.

The deal requires approval from Horizon stockholders and clearance under the Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust act. It includes a $35 million break-up fee plus expenses of up to $5 million if Horizon/CMS ends the pact and is targeted for acquisition by another suitor, the companies said.
Neal Elliott, Horizon's chairman and chief executive, will join HealthSouth's board upon the merger's completion, which is expected in mid-1997, the companies said.
